To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a blockchain for providing an immutable transaction ledger can facilitate a decentralized smart grid.

the combination of decentralization, blockchain, smart contracts, and a universal interface for data access, action invocation, and state modification, can provide the basis for an open, scalable, and privacy-preserving platform for scripting problem solving agents.
the use of a state manipulation based interface, combined with decentralisation, provides the ability to specify and execute complex dynamics in a secure and scalable way.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a universal interface and scripting language for accessing and manipulating data and resources across many systems under different ownership, with the aim of providing increased automation and productivity.
the development of a universal scripting language to specify the behaviour of agents in a decentralised, interconnected, and heterogeneous environment.
a new kind of distributed system, one that is not based on the client server model but rather on the manipulation of resources that can be both virtual and physical, and the interaction between them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a working prototype that demonstrates the feasibility of our approach.
we are working on a language to specify the interaction between resources, and we believe it can be used for problem solving.
the language and framework presented in this thesis provide a solid foundation for the development of problem solving agents for the smart grid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is able to provide a secure, decentralised, flexible, extensible and scalable solution to the problem of scripting agents in a decentralised smart grid.
we provide a framework for scripting smart grid problem solving agents.
we have a language that is expressive enough to describe complex systems, yet simple and easy to use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decentralisation is an essential feature of the abstraction, and that a rule based language is a suitable language for expressing dynamics in this context.
the decentralised nature of the abstraction under study is a key enabler for the envisioned functionality.
the decentralisation of the underlying data and action model provides a key enabler of scale and security.
